book.why: It is the only name two members picked: Ophelia sees it as the purest play on Financials leading under a hawkish Warsh, Cecil as a fortress bank at 16.4x with EPS up 13.4%, and it sits at 98.6% of its 52-week high with the lowest weekly volatility on the sheet (1.57%).

Ophelia and Cecil both want a staple, and PM is the one buyers are backing (+1.9% on the hawkish week, 99.4% of its 52-week high) while Cecil's PEP fell 1.7%, so it is the defensive most likely to hold up whichever way Friday's jobs report breaks.

It beats Cecil's PGR for the second financial slot because card volume does not depend on the yield curve, so it offsets JPM's risk from a soft jobs report instead of repeating PGR's rate bet, and it is less volatile (2.7% a week against 4.45%) while sitting at a record close.

Marky's pullback screen lands in the one sector all three members point to, and UNH, a low-volatility insurer (2.41%), rose 0.7% last week while LLY and REGN fell, so it gives the book healthcare that does not depend on Monday's MFN pricing round.

Cecil's cheapest healthcare name (16.9x, net cash, +25% over 12 weeks) fell 4.8% in the same week as LLY's leak-driven drop, so it should share the rebound Ophelia expects if Monday's MFN round clears, without the GLP-1 exposure that made Cecil skip LLY and that Ophelia names as her own failure mode; it is the smallest position because of that Monday risk.

rationale: JPM is the only name two members reached on their own (Ophelia through sector rotation, Cecil through value), so it takes the 30% cap. The rest of the book stays in Financials, Healthcare and Staples, where the members' views overlap, taking the name with the better one-week setup in each: V over PGR because it hedges JPM's jobs-report risk, PM over PEP because it is the staple buyers are backing, and UNH plus REGN over LLY to keep the healthcare exposure all three want without the GLP-1 terms in Monday's MFN round. Marky's D, SPG and AMD sit in groups Cecil explicitly skipped (utilities, rate-exposed REITs, semis), which the hawkish Warsh repricing hurts; CAT has no support from the other members after an 11% 12-week slide; and META and NUE are single-member picks with 5-7% weekly volatility. Cash is 10% because the week holds two all-or-nothing events, Monday's MFN round and Friday's jobs report ahead of an FOMC that could hike, and the VIX at a 2026 low leaves little cushion; I have no memory of how this week went and used none.
